documents.title: Doc 56 - Decision - Car 41 - Alleged driving opposite direction
documents.subject: Decision - Car 41 - Alleged driving opposite direction

details.competitor: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls F1 Team
details.fact: The Driver drove in the wrong direction at Turn 5
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 12.2.1.h of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 41 (Arvid Lindblad), team representative and reviewed video and in-car video evidence. Car 41 spun after the exit of Turn 5 and was facing towards oncoming cars. Car 41 drove in the wrong direction for approximately 100 metres back to Turn 5 and used the run-off area to turn around. The Driver explained that he could not perform a flick turn from the position in which his car was stopped after the spin. Because he was facing the wrong way, he drove back a short distance against oncoming traffic but staying to the edge of the track and away from the racing line. After he was sure the last car had passed, the Driver of Car 41 attempted a flick turn but the car would not rotate. The Driver explained that, knowing that the last car had passed and it would present no danger for him to continue, he drove back to turn 5 where he knew there would be space to turn. Having regard to the difficult position the Driver of Car 41 found himself in, where his car was originally prone and then unable to turn, and given further that there was no oncoming traffic, the Stewards determined that what occurred was not in these circumstances unsafe and therefore took no further action.

documents.title: Doc 29 - Infringement - Car 3 - Yellow flag infringement
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 3 - Yellow flag infringement

details.fact: Car 3 overtook Car 44 under single yellow flags.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix H, Article 2.5.5b of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: No penalty is applied.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 3 (Max Verstappen), the driver of Car 44 (Lewis Hamilton), team representatives and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video, timing, telemetry, team radio and in-car video evidence. As Car 3 was exiting turn 7 on a push lap, a single yellow flag was displayed. Car 44 was ahead of Car 3 and had been warned of Car 3’s approach. The Driver of Car 44 said that after exiting turn 7, he slowed and moved to the right to ensure he was off the racing line. Car 3 overtook Car 44 prior to turn 8 while both cars were still in the yellow flag sector. Car 3 then abandoned the push lap. The Driver of Car 3 explained that he was on throttle exiting turn 7 and then saw the yellow flag and lifted. This was confirmed by telemetry. Within approximately 40 metres of entering the yellow flag sector, the Driver of Car 3 had lifted fully off throttle. The Driver of Car 44 was braking and had reduced speed to less than 60km/h at the point Car 3 overtook. Because Car 3 was on a push lap and was on throttle out of turn 7 and Car 44 had slowed, the speed differential at the point of the overlap was significant despite the fact that the Driver of Car 3 had also started braking. The Stewards were satisfied that the Driver of Car 3 reacted appropriately to the yellow flag by lifting off throttle and reducing speed. The speed of Car 3 at the overtake point was some 70km/h less than Car 3’s speed on another push lap in the same session. The Driver of Car 3 explained that to have avoided the overtake would have required him to have braked very heavily and he considered to have done so would have potentially created an unsafe situation. The Stewards determined that the Driver of Car 3 breached the yellow flag regulation by overtaking Car 44. However, the Stewards were satisfied that the overtake was an unfortunate consequence of the significant closing speed differential and, in these circumstances, determined not to impose a penalty.

The Stewards have sympathy for the fact that energy management with these cars is extremely difficult, but determine that the driver could have done more to comply with the delta.

documents.title: Doc 53 - Infringement - Car 63 - Leaving the track and gaining an advantage
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 63 - Leaving the track and gaining an advantage

details.fact: Car 63 left the track and repoined gaining a lasting advantage, in Turn 12
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 c) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: 5 second time penalty.
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video, and in-car video evidence, plus submissions from the teams of Cars 63 and 81 via the FIA Evidence Channel. The driver of Car 63 was defending position from Car 81, into Turn 12 and left the track, then proceeded to rejoin in front of Car 81, prior to Turn 13. He retained that position. Accordingly he is determined by the Stewards to have left the track, rejoined it and gained a lasting advantage. The normal penalty for this is a 10 second penalty, however the Stewards considered that the driver of Car 63 had previously been pressuring Car 6 and that put Car 81 into an attacking position (and therefore Car 63 into a defending position). Further, this was a first lap incident and in our determination, the penalty should be mitigated to 5 seconds.

documents.title: Doc 52 - Infringement - Car 87 - Causing a Collision
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 87 - Causing a Collision

details.fact: Car 87 collided with Car 10 in T13.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: 10 second time penalty.
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed video, team radio, in-car video evidence and submissions from the team and the team of Car 10 (Pierre Gasly) via the FIA Evidence Channel. Car 87 (Oliver Bearman) moved to overtake Car 10 at turn 11. The front axle of Car 87 was not ahead of the mirror of Car 10 at the apex where a collision occurred between the two cars. The Stewards determined that the driver of Car 87 was wholly to blame for the collision and imposed a 10 second penalty accordingly.

documents.title: Doc 51 - Decision - Car 5 - Alleged leaving the track and gaining and advantage
documents.subject: Decision - Car 5 - Alleged leaving the track and gaining and advantage

details.fact: Car 5 left the track in turn 11
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article B1.8.6 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video, and in-car video evidence. At the entry to turn 11, Car 5 (Gabriel Bortoleto) moved to overtake Car 43 (Franco Colapinto) on the outside. Car 43 stayed alongside and in that battle Car 5 left the edge of the track and rejoined ahead of Car 43. Under the Driving Standards Guidelines, had the front axle of Car 5 been ahead at the apex, Car 5 would have been entitled to racing room on the inside. There was no racing room on the inside which explained why Car 5 left the edge of the track. Had the front axle of Car 43 been ahead of the front axle of Car 5 at the apex, Car 43 was not obliged to leave racing room on the outside. The Stewards were unable, by reference to the available evidence, to reach a level of comfortable satisfaction as to which of the two cars was ahead at the apex and in these circumstances determined to take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 48 - Infringement - Car 18 - Changes made during Parc Ferme
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 18 - Changes made during Parc Ferme

details.fact: The setup of the suspension has been changed while under parc fermé. The team continued to work on the car beyond the covers off time. The following Power Unit elements have been used: 6th Engine (ICE) 7th Turbocharger (TC) 8th Energy Store (ES) 7th Control Electronics Unit (PU-CE) 9th Power Unit Ancillary Component (PU-ANC) All Power Unit elements were replaced without the approval of the FIA Technical Delegate during parc fermé.
details.infringement: Breaches of Article B8.2.2 (read in conjunction with B8.2.3), B3.4.3a, B3.4.3b, B3.5.3 and B3.5.4 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
details.decision: Required to start the Race from the pit lane.
details.reason: The use of each additional element in this case carries a 5 grid place penalty, therefore there is an accumulation of 25 places. However, as the parts were replaced under parc fermé conditions without the approval of the Technical Delegate a pit lane start is mandated in accordance with Article B3.5.3a of the FIA F1 Regulations. Furthermore, Aston Martin Aramco F1 Team continued to work on Car 18 beyond 2 hours of the end of Qualifying and within 5 hours of the scheduled start of the formation lap of the Race. This is not in accordance with Articles B3.4.3a and B3.4.3b and is deemed to represent a breach of Article B3.5.3 requiring a pit lane start in accordance with Article B3.5.3a of the FIA F1 Regulations. Aston Martin Aramco F1 Team also changed the setup of Car 18 under parc fermé before the start of the Race without the approval of the Technical Delegate. This is not accordance with Article B3.5.4 of the FIA F1 Regulations and, because the change of setup is not in accordance with Article B3.5.3 of the FIA F1 Regulations, for this additional reason Car 18 is required to start the Race from pit lane as per Article B3.5.3a of the FIA F1 Regulations.

documents.title: Doc 41 - Decision - Qualifying SC2-SC1 Times
documents.subject: Decision - Qualifying SC2-SC1 Times

details.fact: The F1 Cars below exceeded the 1:55.0 time limit between the Safety Car lines.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article B1.8.5 of the FIA F1 Regulations and Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code (non-compliance with the Race Director’s Competition Notes, item 1, document 27).
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards thoroughly reviewed Marshalling/Positioning data, timing data, on-board cameras and CCTV cameras. All drivers concerned stayed at or above speeds necessary to stay below 1:55.0 around the vast majority of the circuit. However, in all cases the Stewards determined that the drivers took appropriate actions to not impede other drivers, and in all cases, they slowed down significantly to allow other drivers to pass while giving those drivers a clear track. The Stewards therefore determine that all drivers concerned did not drive “unnecessarily slowly”, and that they were above the maximum time because they took appropriate steps, and we therefore take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 38 - Infringement - Car 5 - Impeding of Car 44
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 5 - Impeding of Car 44

details.fact: Car 5 impeded Car 44 in Turn 12 at 13:22
details.infringement: Breach of Article B4.1.1 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
details.decision: Driver: Warning.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 5 (Gabriel Bortoleto) and the team representatives and reviewed video, team radio and in-car video evidence. When Car 44 was on a push lap approaching turn 12, Car 5, on an in-lap, was travelling at a lower speed in a position which compromised Car 44’s braking. Car 44 had to abort the lap. The driver of Car 5 explained that he had received a warning from his engineer some 15 seconds earlier of Car 44’s approach but he was busy dealing with his car on the approach to turn 12 and overlooked that warning. He received no reminder of Car 44’s approach before turn 12. He explained that because the entry to turn 12 is downhill, he only saw Car 44 at the last moment and released the brakes and went into the run-off area. He agreed that the move was too late and he had compromised Car 44’s lap. Car 44’s team representative acknowledged that the incident was not dangerous. The Stewards determined that Car 5 unnecessarily impeded Car 44 and impose a warning consistent with previous incidents of this type in free practice sessions.

documents.title: Doc 37 - Infringement - Car 6 - Driving erratically
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 6 - Driving erratically

details.fact: Car 6 was driven in a manner that was regarded as erratic following an incident involving Car 23 at Turn1
details.infringement: Breach of Article B1.8.5 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
details.decision: Driver: Formal warning.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 6 (Isack Hadjar), the team representative of Car 6 and reviewed video evidence. On the approach to Turn 1, Car 23 moved to the outside of the corner on the approach of Car 6, to avoid any impeding of that car. The driver of Car 6 locked brakes and had to abort the lap. He was obviously upset with this and took what could be described as “retaliatory action” by swerving towards Car 23. The Stewards regard this as not only erratic but also an action that should be discouraged and hence impose the penalty of a warning to the driver. Had the action been dangerous or resulted in a collision, a more severe penalty would have been imposed.

documents.title: Doc 36 - Infringement - Car 27 - Alleged Pit Lane Incident
documents.subject: Infringement - Car 27 - Alleged Pit Lane Incident

details.fact: Whilst performing a Practice Start, Car 27 pulled out in front of Car 18.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 12.2.1.h of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards heard from the team representative of Car 27 and reviewed video, team radio and in-car video evidence. The team representative explained that the driver’s rear vision was obscured by the car behind at the Practice Start location, and that the driver had no idea of the approach of Car 18. He further explained that the start procedure can take between 5 and 15 seconds so at the time the driver took the decision to commence that procedure, the proximity of Car 18 would not have been obvious to him. The situation was compounded by the fact that the pit lane exit road (as marked) requires cars performing practice starts to merge with cars travelling down the fast lane directly to the pit exit, over a very short distance. The Stewards noted that although the driver of Car 18 had to brake, the situation was determined not to be dangerous and was easily managed by both drivers. Accordingly a decision of No Further Action is taken.
